text: Kyma Bay is a small family-run hotel on the western edge of Chania, set between olive groves and a long sandy beach. The building was a citrus warehouse until the nineteen-seventies, when the grandparents of the current owners turned it into eight simple rooms for travellers. Today the hotel has thirty-two rooms and suites, but it has kept the thick stone walls, the arched doorways and the quiet courtyard where guests still gather in the evening.

Every room opens onto a private balcony or a small garden terrace. The sea view suites on the upper floor look straight across the bay towards the lighthouse, and on clear days you can see the White Mountains behind the town. Beds are made with Cretan cotton, the floors are laid with local terracotta tiles, and each room has air conditioning, a rain shower, a minibar stocked with island products and a desk for those who cannot quite leave work behind.

Breakfast is the meal our guests talk about most. It is served on the terrace from half past seven until half past ten and changes with the seasons: thick yoghurt with thyme honey, warm barley rusks, tomatoes from the garden, soft mizithra cheese, fresh figs in late summer and oranges from our own trees in winter. Eggs are cooked to order, the bread is baked every morning in the village, and the coffee is strong enough to wake even the most tired traveller.

In the evening the taverna serves dishes that our chef learned from her mother and grandmother. Lamb is slow-cooked with artichokes and lemon, snails are fried with rosemary and vinegar, and the vegetable pies are rolled out by hand each afternoon. The wine list is short but carefully chosen, with bottles from small producers in the hills around Kissamos and Heraklion. Reservations are recommended in July and August, when tables on the terrace fill up quickly.

The beach in front of the hotel is sandy and shallow, which makes it a favourite with families who travel with small children. Sunbeds and umbrellas are free for our guests, and towels are waiting at the reception every morning. A lifeguard is on duty from June to September. If you prefer quieter water, the rocky coves a short walk to the west are perfect for snorkelling, and we lend masks and fins at no extra cost.

Chania’s old town is a ten-minute walk along the harbour. Its narrow lanes are full of workshops, bakeries and small shops selling leather, ceramics and herbs from the mountains. Visit the covered market early in the morning, before the day gets hot, and take time to walk out along the breakwater to the Venetian lighthouse. In the evening the waterfront restaurants light their lanterns, and the whole harbour smells of grilled fish and jasmine.

For those who want to explore further, the reception can arrange car hire, boat trips and guided walks. The Samaria Gorge is one of the longest in Europe and takes most walkers between five and seven hours; we prepare a packed lunch if you leave before breakfast. Balos lagoon, with its pale pink sand and turquoise water, is best reached by boat from Kissamos. In spring the hills above the hotel are covered with wild flowers, and our gardener is happy to point out the best paths.

Our small spa sits in the old cellar of the building. It has a heated indoor pool, a steam room and two treatment rooms where our therapists offer massages with olive oil, sea salt and local herbs. Treatments should be booked at least a day in advance. The spa is open every day from ten in the morning until eight in the evening, and it is reserved for adults after six, so that guests who want a quiet hour can enjoy it in peace.

We care deeply about the island and try to run the hotel in a way that respects it. The water in every room is heated by solar panels on the roof, the garden is watered with collected rainwater, and most of what we serve comes from farms within thirty kilometres. We have stopped using plastic bottles in the rooms and offer refillable glass bottles instead. Guests who stay five nights or longer can choose to skip daily cleaning, and we plant an olive tree for every such stay.

Check-in starts at three in the afternoon and check-out is until eleven in the morning. If you arrive early, you are welcome to leave your luggage at the reception and start your holiday on the beach. Late check-out can be arranged when the room is free, for a small fee. Airport transfers are available at any hour; please send us your flight number at least two days before you arrive, so that our driver can wait for you even if the plane is delayed.

Children of all ages are welcome. Children under six stay free of charge when they share their parents’ room, and cots and high chairs are available on request. The garden has a shaded play area, and on summer evenings we show films for families in the courtyard. Pets are welcome in the garden rooms only, because those rooms have their own entrance and a small fenced terrace. Please let us know in advance if you plan to travel with a dog or a cat.

Cancellation is free until fourteen days before arrival. After that date we charge the first night, unless we can sell the room to another guest. Bookings made directly on our website always receive the best available price, a bottle of local wine on arrival and a discount at the spa. If you have any questions before you travel, please call us or write to us: the same family has answered every message for fifty years, and we look forward to welcoming you to Kyma Bay.

Getting here is easy. Chania airport is twenty-five minutes away by car, and the ferry from Piraeus arrives in Souda every morning after an overnight crossing. Buses to the town centre stop at the end of our lane every half hour during the day. If you drive, follow the coast road west from the harbour and turn left after the second bridge, at the sign with the blue wave. Parking is free for our guests, and there are two charging points for electric cars next to the garden. We will gladly send you a map before you travel.
